Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L01_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.03

Which choice best shows ethos in a speech?

answer.text: A. A speaker says, Everyone feels nervous sometimes

feedback.text: This focuses on emotion, so it is closer to pathos

answer.text: B. A speaker says, As a trained peer mentor, I have helped students practice introductions

feedback.text: Correct. This builds credibility because the speaker shows relevant experience

answer.text: C. A speaker lists three facts about speech timing

feedback.text: Facts and measurable support are logos, not ethos

answer.text: D. A speaker uses a metaphor about confidence

feedback.text: Figurative language can help style, but it does not automatically build credibility

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L01_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Which choice best shows pathos in a speech?

answer.text: A. A speaker cites a research study about memory

feedback.text: Research evidence is logos because it depends on logic and facts

answer.text: B. A speaker explains professional experience with presentations

feedback.text: Experience builds ethos because it supports credibility

answer.text: C. A speaker asks the audience to remember the relief of finishing a hard task

feedback.text: Correct. This appeals to emotion by asking listeners to connect with a feeling

answer.text: D. A speaker defines the word rehearsal

feedback.text: A definition may clarify meaning, but it does not create emotional appeal

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L01_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.07

Which choice best shows logos in a speech?

answer.text: A. A speaker uses data to show that organized notes improve timing

feedback.text: Correct. This is logos because data gives logical support for the claim

answer.text: B. A speaker shares a personal credential

feedback.text: A credential supports ethos because it builds trust

answer.text: C. A speaker describes fear before speaking

feedback.text: Fear appeals to emotion, so it is closer to pathos

answer.text: D. A speaker says practice is a bridge

feedback.text: That phrase is figurative language, not evidence by itself

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L01_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.03

Which choice best shows figurative language?

answer.text: A. Practice improves delivery when students rehearse

feedback.text: This is a literal statement, not figurative language

answer.text: B. Students should practice before the speech

feedback.text: This gives advice but does not create a nonliteral image

answer.text: C. The speaker has three main points

feedback.text: This describes structure, not figurative language

answer.text: D. Practice is the bridge between nervousness and confidence

feedback.text: Correct. This metaphor compares practice to a bridge to make the idea memorable

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L01_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Which choice best shows speaker purpose?

answer.text: A. The speech has words in it

feedback.text: This is too vague and does not identify purpose

answer.text: B. The speaker wants the audience to believe rehearsal is useful

feedback.text: Correct. This identifies what the speaker wants the audience to understand

answer.text: C. The speaker talks for a while

feedback.text: Length is not the same as communication purpose

answer.text: D. The audience sits quietly

feedback.text: Audience behavior is not the speaker purpose
